source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-36

procedures.title: A/C component replacement: preparing the system
steps: After a compressor mechanical failure, take the compressor out.
Take out the receiver-dehydrator and scrap it.
Flush the condenser to clear out debris pumped into it.
Disconnect the receiver-dehydrator line at the expansion valve inlet and check the inlet screen for metal chips or debris; replace the screen if plugged, then reconnect the line.
Fit a new receiver-dehydrator.
Fit the replacement compressor.
Add oil: 1 fluid oz. for the new receiver-dehydrator plus the amount the replacement compressor needs (see Checking Compressor Oil Charge).
Evacuate and charge the system.
Check system performance.

procedures.title: Refrigerant line O-ring connections: service
steps: Fit a new O-ring every time a connection is opened.
Dip the new O-ring in clean refrigeration oil before fitting.
Hold the fitting with a backing wrench so the pipe does not twist and damage the O-ring.
Tighten to the table torque; do not overtighten.

procedures.title: Refrigerant hose clamp connections: install and remove
steps: Install: coat the tube and hose with clean refrigeration oil.
Push the hose over the three sealing beads until it butts against the fourth (locating) bead; use no sealer.
Fit the clamps with their locating arms hooked over the cut end of the hose.
Tighten the clamp screw to 35-42 lb. in.; do not retighten afterwards.
Remove: with a sharp knife, make an angled cut in the hose (see figure 38 in the manual) to loosen it, then work it off the fitting.
Trim off the slit end of the hose before refitting, and reinstall as above.
notes: Clamp torque normally drops as the hose settles; only retorque if it has fallen below 10 lb. in., and then to 20-25 lb. in. More may damage the hose.
Caution: use only approved refrigeration hose, never heater hose. Do not nick or score the sealing beads when cutting off a hose; a lengthwise cut risks this.

procedures.title: Refrigerant leak at O-ring connection: repair
steps: Check the fitting torque and tighten to spec if loose, using a backing wrench; do not overtighten. Leak test again.
If it still leaks, discharge the refrigerant
